chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Atlantic City musicians: Egg Harbor Club, Claude Hopkins's small band
summary: He recalls the good musicians in Atlantic City, Charlie Taylor's band at the Egg Harbor Club, and the small instrumentation of the Hopkins band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Claude Hopkins band -- it's a little club down there. I ran across -- there's been a lot of good musicians in Philly at that time -- in Atlantic City at that time. There was the Egg Harbor Club there with a great band in it, and there was Charlie Taylor, the colored violinist -- they had a great band out at Egg Harbor. Big band there. And you had a chance to really here -- as young as I was, I heard some great musicians down there in Atlantic City. Then I have to go back home -- go back to school, you know.
You were still in high school at this time.
I see. So, the Claude Hopkins Band was shortly after he returned from overseas.
Yeah. He had a fine band. A little small band. It wasn't too big. It was like two saxophones, rhythm, and maybe a trumpet. Most of those bands had banjos, and I
